issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s customary right of pre-emption, acquired by virtue of a heritable tenancy, is heritable.
material_facts: A tenant in possession of part of a building claimed a customary right of pre-emption arising from his tenancy and filed a suit to enforce it.
The tenant died while the suit was pending.
The tenancy itself was heritable, and the claimed pre-emption right was incidental to that tenancy.
issues.conclusion: The customary right of pre-emption acquired by virtue of the tenancy was heritable.
issues.legal_principle: A right of pre-emption does not itself create an interest in immovable property, but a right attached to or incidental to a heritable tenancy should ordinarily be heritable. There is no relevant distinction between a right of pre-emption arising under statute and one arising under customary law. The Court applied Hazari v. Neki, followed Wajid Ali v. Shaban, referred to Faqir Ali Shah v. Ram Kishan, and overruled the contrary holding in Chandrup Singh v. Data Ram concerning a statutory right under section 15(1) of the Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1913.

predicates.preemption_proceeding: The case is a proceeding to enforce a claimed right of pre-emption.
predicates.customary_tenant_right: A tenant claims a customary right of pre-emption by virtue of occupying the property as a tenant.
predicates.heritable_tenancy: The tenancy from which the claimed right arises is heritable.
predicates.tenant_preemption_right_is_heritable: The tenant’s pre-emption right is capable of passing to the tenant’s heirs.

issues.definition: When a pre-emption proceeding concerns a customary right arising from a heritable tenancy, the tenant’s pre-emption right is heritable.

issues.legal_issue: The legal representatives of a tenant who dies during a suit to enforce a customary pre-emption right may be substituted and continue the suit when the right to sue survives.
material_facts: The tenant filed a suit to enforce a customary right of pre-emption arising from his tenancy.
The tenant died while the suit was pending, before a decree had been granted.
His legal representatives applied to be substituted so they could prosecute the suit, and the trial court allowed the application.
issues.conclusion: The right to sue survived to the tenant’s legal representatives, who were entitled to be substituted under Order 22, Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure and continue the suit.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order 22, Rule 3 of the Code of Civil Procedure, legal representatives may be substituted when the right to sue survives. Because the pre-emption right was incidental to a heritable tenancy, the tenant’s death during trial did not extinguish the right to sue. The Court followed Hazari v. Neki, held Chandrup Singh v. Data Ram inconsistent with that decision and overruled it, and distinguished Muhammad Husain v. Niamet-un-nissa as involving a different basis for the claimed right.

rule.if: preemption_suit and plaintiff_died_while_suit_pending and right_to_sue_is_heritable and applicants_are_legal_representatives

predicates.preemption_suit: The proceeding is a suit to enforce a right of pre-emption.
predicates.plaintiff_died_while_suit_pending: The plaintiff died before the suit was finally decided.
predicates.right_to_sue_is_heritable: The right underlying the suit survives the plaintiff’s death and passes to the plaintiff’s heirs.
predicates.applicants_are_legal_representatives: The persons seeking substitution are the deceased plaintiff’s legal representatives.
predicates.legal_representatives_may_be_substituted: The legal representatives are entitled to replace the deceased plaintiff and prosecute the suit.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff in a pre-emption suit dies while it is pending, the right to sue is heritable, and the applicants are the plaintiff’s legal representatives, they may be substituted and continue the suit.
